  "surface_mechanism_description": "The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of trimethylaluminum (TMA) and the subsequent reaction with oxygen radicals and ions generated by plasma. The process includes the formation of surface hydroxyl groups and the desorption of byproducts such as methane and hydrogen.",
  "intermediate_species": ["surface hydroxyls", "oxygen radicals", "oxygen ions"],
  "evidence": "In the PEALD process of oxide films, oxygen radicals and ions are used as the oxidants and thus it is possible to enhance the reactivity of a reactant gas. The use of PEALD in growing Al2O3 films for the insulator of electroluminescent display has contributed to stable device operation due to the improved breakdown field of the insulating layer. The growth rates of PEALD Al2O3 films were higher than those of ALD and an increase in the growth temperature from 150 to 350°C was accompanied by a steady decrease in the growth rates for PEALD while a constant growth rate was obtained for ALD. The higher growth rate for the PEALD Al2O3 may be ascribed to the reactive species of the oxygen source achieving a higher density of available adsorption and packing sites, which also resulted in improving the film density."
